model_output.score_comment_long: Leading a team of 40 gives the current role a useful anchor. Most other bullets name broad duties without explaining what you changed or handled. Add details to the fulfillment, process improvement, and scanning system bullets first.
model_output.score_plain: A reviewer can place you in operations management, but may struggle to distinguish your work from a standard job description. More detail about specific changes and responsibilities would make comparisons easier.
model_output.first_impression: The move from Team Lead to Operations Manager is easy to follow. Leading 40 people is worth keeping near the top because it makes the current management role concrete.

model_output.summary: Your progression runs from a parcel sorting line to managing fulfillment operations. The current title and team size point to an operations manager, while the earlier scanning rollout and scheduling work add floor-level context. The resume says you improved department processes, but doesn't describe the changes, so a reviewer can't tell what kind of operational problems you addressed.
strengths: The Team Lead, Assistant Operations Manager, and Operations Manager titles make your progression through operations roles easy to trace.
The scanning system rollout shows involvement in a change on the floor, not just routine coverage.
Scheduling, reporting, Excel, and WMS give a reader a starting point for understanding your administrative and systems exposure.
gaps: The fulfillment bullet doesn't identify which parts of daily operations you oversaw, so the boundaries of the manager role remain unclear.
The leadership planning bullet doesn't say what goals you contributed to or what you brought to those discussions.
The scanning rollout doesn't explain your contribution, making it difficult to understand how you supported the change.
